observations: A roughly oval head fills the center against a flat hot-pink background; five pointed spike shapes rise from the top edge, rendered in teal, white, and green lines.

Two eye zones are built from sharp triangular and diamond outlines in white and yellow, with deep red fill visible inside each, creating hard angular contrast against surrounding dense cross-hatched marks.

The lower face carries a wide open mouth outlined in pink and red, showing blocky tooth forms; the entire head surface is layered with short overlapping strokes in black, lime green, orange, teal, and brown.
reading: The flat pink field holds the head at a fixed distance, giving it nowhere to recede. Inside that stillness the surface is anything but quiet: dense cross-hatched strokes in green, orange, and black press against each other without resolving into smooth form. The angular eye shapes read as confrontational—not because the face scowls, but because hard geometry inside soft scribble creates a visual standoff. The open mouth adds a second point of tension without tipping into legible expression.
contextAngle: Within the owned nifty-faces subset, #15 sits between nnxyz nifty faces #14 and nnxyz nifty faces #16 in both title and recorded creation order. Against #14's yellow ground and rectangular framing, and #16's dispersed angular fragments, #15 holds its marks in one contained oval on pink.

connections.reason: Both works center a single dense head with angular eye constructions over layered cross-hatching, but #14 uses a yellow ground and rectangular framing while #15 uses hot pink and a rounder, spikier silhouette—making the contrast in ground color and outer shape directly visible.

nnxyz nifty faces #16 shares the same multi-color cross-hatched line vocabulary but disperses the face into broken angular fragments across a yellow field, whereas #15 keeps all that mark density compressed into one contained oval—a clear formal contrast between cohesion and dispersal.

lookingQuestion: The triangular eye outlines sit inside a surface of curved, overlapping short strokes—where exactly does the angular geometry end and the surrounding mark-making begin, and does that boundary hold consistently across both eyes?
ambiguities: The nnotb #192 comparison image shows an open composition with a teal ground and spiral eye forms; no strong formal parallel to #15 was found, so it was inspected but not selected.

Title-derived order and recorded creation order align for this work and its immediate neighbors in the owned subset, but gaps elsewhere in the family mean this cannot be extended to a broader sequence claim.
